A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLVR reasoning-boundary study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the relocated discussion and relabeled appendices.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix D report original benchmark evaluations, controlled RL training comparisons, ablations, manual chain-of-thought checks, and perplexity analyses.

after.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendix C retain the work's original benchmark evaluations, controlled RL experiments, ablations, and reasoning analyses.

M1.justification: The evaluation approach, RL algorithms, training objectives, and model procedures are unchanged. Curriculum learning, process rewards, and agentic exploration in the expanded discussion are future directions, not implemented method additions.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage remains unchanged across mathematics, coding, and visual reasoning, including AIME24/25, Omni-MATH, LiveCodeBench, and the visual mathematics benchmarks. The newly discussed curriculum and agentic scenarios are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same model pairs and comparators. Table 3 still compares PPO, GRPO, ReMax, RLOO, Reinforce++, and DAPO; Figure 7 retains base, RL, instruction-tuned, and distilled models. Newly cited methods are not added baselines.

E3.justification: The default temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.95, generation limits, prompts, filtering procedures, and training settings are retained. Section 4.3 also retains the 2,000/821 Omni-MATH training/test split. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The chain-of-thought checks, coverage and perplexity analyses, KL/rollout ablations, temperature and entropy comparisons, training dynamics, and model-scaling analysis are retained. Appendix D's experimental material becomes Appendix C without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the same unbiased pass@k estimator and sample-count conventions. Perplexity distribution reporting is unchanged, and no new seed replication, confidence intervals, or significance tests appear. Figure 8's added sampling-efficiency gaps are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Figure 8 newly states six numerical sampling-efficiency gaps: 0.359, 0.410, and 0.206 above; 0.247, 0.408, and 0.199 below. These add numerical summaries of existing evaluations; the underlying curves and Tables 2–6 retain their results.

T1.justification: The RL objective, PPO surrogate, GRPO/RLOO advantage definitions, pass@k estimator, perplexity formula, and sampling-efficiency-gap definition are unchanged. The expanded discussion introduces no formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Headline summaries in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion change 'does not' elicit novel reasoning to 'rarely'; the introduction now says reasoning coverage is 'often' narrower. These qualify generality while retaining the main sampling-efficiency, base-model-bound, and distillation claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands the former Appendix C discussion by emphasizing token-level exploration and binary outcome rewards, and explaining curriculum/meta-skill and process-reward remedies. Section 7 explicitly qualifies the conclusions through proprietary-model access constraints and rapidly evolving RLVR techniques.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, estimator details, and all training/evaluation prompt templates are retained, including Appendix A and v3 Appendix E/v5 Appendix D. The work's project-page and implementation access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Adds references including AlphaEvolve, StepHint, Questa, AceReason-Nemotron, and IMO verification/refinement to support future directions, plus Absolute Zero and Beyond the 80/20 Rule in Appendix B. Positioning against earlier RLVR analyses remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Moves and expands the appendix discussion into main-text Section 5, renumbers subsequent sections and appendices, adds Author Contributions, and changes the conclusion to Conclusion and Limitations. Wording edits and reorganization are localized; the core exposition is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 8 adds dashed reference lines, gap arrows, and numerical annotations. Other figures and tables retain their displays, with localized reflow such as Figure 12 moving from v3 page 19 to v5 page 21.

improvement.justification: v5 modestly reduces overstatement in headline summaries and makes the discussion and applicability qualifications more explicit in Sections 5 and 7. These improve interpretation, although categorical base-model-bound statements remain elsewhere and the underlying empirical evidence is unchanged.
